title: Effectiveness of Generate→Validate→Repair with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does integrating a Batfish-based validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by LLM intent-to-configuration translation compared to LLM-only generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) produces a lower per-task rate of validator-detected configuration errors than LLM-only generation (baseline).
H2 (secondary): Under the preregistered model-call budget and repair bound (≤3 repairs), the automated repair loop will correct >50% of initial validator-detected errors (repair success rate > 50%).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do vendor-like syntax strata (IOS-like vs JunOS-like) and complexity strata (single-rule vs multi-step changes) moderate the pipeline benefit?
EQ2: What failure modes remain after repair (verifier-unchecked regressions, semantic misinterpretations), as categorized by an automated failure taxonomy?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic multi-vendor topologies and templates released with the artifact (sandbox-only; non-production).
Validator-in-the-loop tests limited to sandbox semantics verifiable by Batfish and an independent static reachability checker implemented in the experiment harness.
model_scope: Hosted LLM API (single model family) pre-registered as hosted_llm_v1 for this run; exact provider/model identifier and API version will be recorded immutably in the execution manifest and Disclosure Statement.
All prompts, prompt variants, and random seeds are preregistered (see Analysis Plan).
transformation_scope: Deterministic vendor-template rendering and canonicalization (syntax normalization) applied to all generated configurations prior to validator ingestion.
Automatic sanitization rules to remove non-sandbox-capable commands (see Transformation Validation Plan).
secondary_estimands: repair_success_rate (fraction of tasks with initial validator-detected errors where final config is validator-clean)
per-stratum paired success-rate differences (IOS-like vs JunOS-like; single-step vs multi-step)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks (paired design). For each task we obtain two condition outputs: (A) LLM-only generation (one model call) and (B) guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair bounded to 3 repair iterations). Thus: 200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 configuration-generation episodes; pipeline episodes include up to 4 model calls each (1 initial + up to 3 repairs). Vendor and complexity stratification: 4 strata (IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with balanced assignment: 50 tasks per stratum = 200 total. Inclusion: tasks derived from the public task corpus released with artifacts; exclusion: tasks whose canonicalized intent maps to unsupported features in Batfish scenario (pre-declared and removed before execution). All task selection and randomization seeds are preregistered.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis: paired binary outcome per task defined as 'validator-detected error present' (1) vs 'validator-clean' (0) on the final artifact. Use the supplied analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' to compute the estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Primary test: McNemar's test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) on paired binary outcomes. Estimate absolute risk reduction with 95% bootstrap CIs (paired bootstrap with 10,000 resamples). Secondary analyses: compute repair_success_rate with bootstrap CIs; per-stratum paired analyses reported as exploratory with unadjusted p-values. All modeling code, exact prompt texts, seeds, and raw validator outputs are archived; analysis is fully automated using the registered analysis executor. Technical failures (API/infra) are handled per the missingness policy below; sensitivity analysis treats failed pairs as baseline-errors (worst-case).
multiplicity_plan: Single primary endpoint (paired validator-detected error reduction). Exploratory subgroup analyses (4 strata) are explicitly labeled exploratory. No multiplicity adjustment for exploratory analyses in the confirmatory claim. If a small set of pre-planned secondary confirmatory endpoints is later promoted, we will adjust via Holm-Bonferroni; current preregistration contains only the single primary confirmatory test.
missingness_plan: Technical/infrastructure failures: primary analysis uses 'complete-pair' policy: exclude any task pair where either condition failed to produce a usable configuration due to technical failure (API outage, harness crash). A sensitivity analysis will re-run the primary estimand with the conservative assumption that any failed generation in the guarded arm is treated as a validator-detected error (failed_call_treatment: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). All failure events and counts are reported with reasons and hashes.

risk_factors: Verifier-overfitting: repairs may satisfy Batfish checks while introducing other regressions not captured by the verifier.
Sandbox semantic mismatch vs production vendor quirks.
Training-data leakage (models may memorize public templates).
Sensitive or exploitable command generation (dual-use risk).
detection_procedures: Automated Batfish scenario runs for reachability, ACL/policy violations, routing-loop detection, and interface-state regressions (batch, deterministic).

Independent static reachability checker (graph-based reachability analyzer implemented in the harness) run on canonicalized configs to detect obvious semantic divergences not covered by Batfish scenarios.
Automated regex-based dangerous-command detector to flag commands not permitted in sandbox topologies (e.g., out-of-band management, credential configuration).
Repository-wide diff checks: compare pre- and post-repair AST-like command sets to detect large semantic deltas.
item_flagging_rules: If Batfish or static checker detects a 'harm' property (reachability break, loop, or ACL violation), the item is counted as validator-detected error.

If regex-based dangerous-command detector matches, the item is excluded from public release artifacts and flagged; excluded items remain in internal analysis but are withheld from public corpus to avoid dual-use.
If parser/canonicalizer fails on generated config, that pair is recorded as a technical failure and treated per missingness_plan.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis uses Batfish-defined validator-detected error as the outcome. Items flagged by dangerous-command detector are retained in the internal analysis but removed from any public release artifacts; the extent of such removals is reported. Sensitivity analyses report results with and without flagged items.
residual_uncertainty: Residual uncertainty in how well Batfish scenarios emulate production device semantics.
Possibility of undetected semantic regressions outside the pre-registered harm-oracle checks.

budget_scenarios.description: Lower-budget confirmatory run: 100 paired tasks (50 per vendor/complexity pairs balanced).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 100 tasks × 2 conditions = 200 episodes. Baseline: 1 call/episode = 100 calls. Guarded pipeline worst-case: up to 4 calls/episode × 100 = 400 calls. Total planned model calls = 100 + 400 = 500, within capability_manifest max_model_calls (10000).

budget_scenarios.description: Full preregistered confirmatory run: 200 paired tasks (balanced across 4 strata). RECOMMENDED.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes. Baseline: 1 call/episode = 200 calls. Guarded pipeline worst-case: up to 4 calls/episode × 200 = 800 calls. Total planned model calls = 200 + 800 = 1000, well below capability_manifest maximum of 10000 and within the specified estimated_model_calls (2000) in the original candidate record.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points in validator-detected error rate (guarded minus baseline)
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal approximation-based paired-sample discordant-rate approximation for McNemar: n ≈ (z_{α/2}+z_{β})^2 * (p12 + p21) / effect^2; discordant-pair proportion (p12+p21) assumed 0.25 for calculation.
assumptions: Assumed discordant-pair proportion (p12 + p21) = 0.25; target effect = 0.10 (10 p.p.).
Independent tasks; balanced stratification across 4 strata.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired tasks and assumed discordant proportion 0.25, the design detects an absolute paired difference ≈10 percentage points with ~80% power (approximation: (1.96+0.84)^2*0.25/0.10^2 ≈196).
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute minimum detectable effect for discordant rates = 0.15 and 0.35 (lower/higher discordance).
Report achieved power post-hoc given observed discordant rate.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip parse: generated config → AST → serialized config → parse again; failure causes automatic rejection.

Automated diff of pre- and post-transformation ASTs to ensure transformation only normalizes syntax and does not add/remove policy-relevant statements; large structural changes (>10% AST node insert/delete) trigger automated audit sampling.
Deterministic canonical ordering of statements where order is semantically irrelevant (documented rules).
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated config from release if parser failure occurs or if sanitization removes >5% of commands (indicates incompatible generation).
Reject public release of any config matching dangerous-command detector; such items remain in internal analysis but omitted from public corpus.
Reject configurations with unresolvable placeholders or vendor-unsupported features as technical failures.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deep-audit on 10% random sample of outputs per stratum: run canonicalizer round-trip, AST-diff threshold checks, and independent static reachability checks. Audit is deterministic and logged with hashes; failures trigger integration-test re-runs on the pipeline harness.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Intent-to-configuration mapping validated by unit tests against 50 seed template cases covering common constructs; mapping tests are deterministic fixtures embedded in the repo and run in CI prior to data collection.
residual_risks: Canonicalization heuristics may not cover all vendor corner-cases; residual semantic drift possible.
Automated sanitization may remove commands that are benign in production semantics but match conservative disallowed patterns.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Degree to which Batfish sandbox semantics match production device quirks (external-validity; study explicitly bounded to sandbox verification).
Potential for repair-overfitting: repairs that satisfy Batfish checks but introduce other operational regressions not covered by the preregistered harm-oracle.
Prompt/model-call nondeterminism across provider-side model-version changes; we mitigate by recording exact provider/model id and seeds at run-time in the execution manifest.
Generalisability beyond the included vendor-like syntaxes and synthetic topologies (study scope intentionally bounded).
Possibility of training-data leakage leading to inflated performance on publicly derivable templates; artifact release will include provenance and duplicate-detection hashes.
